title: Trade-Offs: Time, Memory, Simplicity, and Readability
learningObjectives: Explain the topic and its assumptions.
Describe why it matters in solving programming problems.
Interpret a small example or trace.
Apply the idea to a new situation.

understand.concept: Design choices balance speed, memory, clarity, maintainability, and risk. Faster approaches may use extra storage; a simple approach may be best for small data. Optimize only after requirements and correctness are understood and the bottleneck is relevant.
understand.whyItMatters: The best solution meets constraints and is understandable, not merely theoretically fastest.
understand.analogy: A reusable tool saves effort later but requires storage and setup; a simple tool can be enough for one task.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy simplifies the concept; real behavior depends on input, constraints, and implementation details.

explain.narrative: Define the task and assumptions, choose a method, trace it on a small example, then check edge cases. Design choices balance speed, memory, clarity, maintainability, and risk. Faster approaches may use extra storage; a simple approach may be best for small data. Optimize only after requirements and correctness are understood and the bottleneck is relevant.
